Day by Day

Built from the finalized guide plus confirmed flight/train bookings. Two scheduling conflicts in the original card-by-card guide are resolved here: Casa Carmela moved off Saturday (it clashed with the Sorsi e Morsi carb-load lunch) to Thursday; Barcelona's Tuesday arrival dinner settled on La Flauta over Cerveseria Catalana (moved to Wednesday).

  1. 🛬
    Sun Nov 29 — Arrival
    Madrid, low-effort day
    Land 9:30 AM (body clock ~3:30 AM NY time — real jet lag). Taxi to Hotel Eurostars Central, bags at the desk if room isn't ready. One easy thing only: Gran Vía Stroll to Puerta del Sol, lunch at Mercado de San Miguel. Back to the hotel to rest before dinner. Casa Salvador is closed today regardless — don't plan around it. Dinner: La Casa del Abuelo or something equally zero-effort.
  2. ☀️
    Mon Nov 30
    Madrid, sightseeing-exterior day
    Many food spots closed Mondays. Royal Palace façade + Sabatini Gardens + Almudena Cathedral (flat, no tickets). Morning coffee: La Cabra Café & Bakery (new, confirm it's open) or Toma Café as fallback. Dinner: Celso y Manolo (reservation essential).
  3. 🌆
    Tue Dec 1 — last full Madrid evening
    Madrid
    Retiro Park (taxi to Puerta de Alcalá gate), stop at Bombonería La Pajarita (Calle de Villanueva 14) for candy/souvenirs on the same taxi trip. Templo de Debod at sunset (~5:50 PM). Descalzas Reales only if legs are fresh — not wheelchair accessible, partial circulation only. Dinner: Casa Salvador — the slot it was built for.
  4. 🚆
    Wed Dec 2 — travel to Valencia
    Madrid → Valencia
    Grab chocolate palmeras from La Duquesita for the train. Taxi to Madrid-Atocha for AVE 05890, 9:42 AM → Valencia J. Sorolla 11:43 AM (confirmed, paid). Light daytime train, minimal fatigue — use the afternoon: settle into the Airbnb, walk the Turia Gardens circuit, coffee at Bluebell Coffee. Dinner: Docemil en Rusia, two minutes from the door — first-night pick.
  5. 🎽
    Thu Dec 3 — Expo day
    Valencia
    Morning: Expo Deporte Valencia, bib pickup (mandatory this week, no race-day pickup). Lunch: Casa Carmela at Malvarrosa Beach, paired with the flat promenade walk. Evening: Alenar.
  6. 🏛️
    Fri Dec 4 — Old Town day
    Valencia
    Morning: Mercado Central (closed Sun, so this is one of two real windows). Midday: La Tòfona for paella (replaces the now-closed Palace Fesol — call ahead). Afternoon: Old Town Flat Stroll, Valencia Cathedral & the Holy Chalice chapel, San Nicolás Church if time allows. Merienda: Horchatería Santa Catalina.
  7. 🍝
    Sat Dec 5 — Race eve
    Valencia
    Morning: light shakeout on the Turia Gardens 5K circuit. Lunch: Sorsi e Morsi, the real carb-load (book ahead). Keep the evening light — no new restaurant experiments the night before a marathon. Lay out race kit, confirm the 8:15 AM start and the Alameda-station race-morning route.
  8. 🏃
    Sun Dec 6 — RACE DAY
    Valencia Marathon
    8:15 AM first wave at Plaça de la Marató. Mom: breakfast at Fornelino Ruzafa, then Plaça de l'Ajuntament (km 30, ~13-min walk) around 9:45 AM, then taxi to the City of Arts finish. Post-race: Rausell for the Sunday celebration lunch (taxi ~8 min) — hours still unconfirmed, call ahead.
  9. 🧘
    Mon Dec 7 — Rest day
    Valencia
    Albufera/El Palmar excursion: Bon Aire (book ahead) or backup Restaurante Mateu. Post-race treat run to DDL Boutique or Dulce de Leche. Low-key, no fresh-legs activity required.
  10. 🚆
    Tue Dec 8 — travel day
    Valencia → Barcelona
    ⚠️ Early start: Euromed 01072, Valencia-Estació del Nord 6:30 AM → Barcelona Sants 9:39 AM (confirmed, paid). Taxi to the station booked the night before. Arrive, taxi straight to Hotel Acta Splendid. Immaculate Conception holiday — slow Gothic Quarter stroll + Barcelona Cathedral + Plaça Catalunya if legs allow; let the legs set the pace. Dinner: La Flauta, 3-minute walk.
  11. 🛍️
    Wed Dec 9
    Barcelona
    Morning: La Boqueria before 10 AM. Afternoon: Barceloneta Promenade. Pre-dinner: quick stand-up bite at Quimet & Quimet in Poble Sec (taxi ~10 min, no seats — a 15-20 min stop for you and Joanne, not a destination for Mom). Evening: Cerveseria Catalana.
  12. ⛪
    Thu Dec 10 — Sagrada Família
    Barcelona
    ✅ 10:00 AM entry confirmed (2 General + 1 Senior, locator 111221232) — non-transferable, bring photo ID. Afterward: Passeig de Gràcia past Casa Batlló and La Pedrera. Dinner: Can Vallés (splurge, reservations essential) or Taktika Berri.
  13. ✈️
    Fri Dec 11 — departure
    Barcelona → home
    Morning fuel: Forn Mistral for ensaïmada. TAP 1033 Barcelona 12:35 PM → Lisbon → JFK 8:05 PM. Remember: depart Newark outbound, land JFK on return.

🎟️ Buy in advance

  • Sagrada Família (Barcelona) — ONLINE-ONLY timed tickets, no walk-up entry. €26 entry / €30 with guided tour at sagradafamilia.org. Buy now — dates release ~60 days out. Skip the tower add-on (lift up but ~300 steps down).
  • Descalzas Reales Monastery (Madrid) — guided visits only, small groups, book online at Patrimonio Nacional. Closed Mondays. It's Mom's call, and only if she's up for several flights of stairs: the ~1-hour tour covers three floors linked only by stairs (it starts up the grand staircase), with no lift or step-free route — Patrimonio Nacional itself states there is currently no access for people with disabilities. Patrimonio's own tour is Spanish-guided and there's no standard Tuesday English slot, so an English visit on Tue Dec 1 needs a third-party/private booking (third-party English tours run Thu/Fri).
  • San Nicolás Church (Valencia) — "Valencia's Sistine Chapel," ticketed entry (~€16), closed Mondays. Book online.
  • Valencia Cathedral — buy online to skip the line (€8–10, includes the Holy Chalice chapel). Fine at the door on a December weekday.
  • Oceanogràfic (Valencia) — timed online tickets, only if Mom wants the aquarium.
  • The two Renfe trains — fares rise as seats sell; still to book.

Madrid

Sun Nov 29 – Wed Dec 2 · Chueca, just above Gran Vía

Home base Hotel Eurostars Central Nov 29 – Dec 2Triple room · elevator ▾

Calle de Mejía Lequerica 10, Chueca/Justicia. Flat streets all around, guest location score 9.2 — Tribunal metro ~250 m away, Gran Vía a 5-minute walk, Puerta del Sol 12–15 flat minutes. A neighborhood-feeling base that keeps walking light for Mom. Everything below is measured from here.

Must Book 1

Casa Salvador 🚶 9 min★ 4.6 ▾

🕐 Lunch Mon–Sat 1:15–4:00 PM · Dinner Tue–Sat 8:15–11:00 PM · Closed Sundays (confirmed via the restaurant's own reservation calendar: Sundays are greyed out/unbookable, Mon–Sat are open)

Old-school Chueca dining room open since 1941 — white-jacket waiters, checkered tablecloths, zero pretension. The featherlight fried hake (merluza) is Wil & Joanne's order; the rabo de toro (oxtail stew) is for Mom. Book for Tuesday night, your last full evening; it's shut on arrival Sunday.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps

Local Gem 5

Bodega de la Ardosa 🚶 7 min★ 4.5 ▾

🕐 Daily 11:00 AM–5:00 PM & 7:00 PM–12:00 AM (Fri–Sat until 1:00 AM) — split hours, closed mid-afternoon

Malasaña tavern pouring since 1892, all tiles and worn wood, just north of the hotel. Vermouth on tap and the tortilla de patatas are the pescatarian orders; the croquetas (jamón) are Mom's. One catch: no reservations and mostly standing room — treat this as a Wil-and-Joanne stand-up vermouth stop, not a sit-down meal for Mom. Arrive by 1:00–1:30 PM on a weekday for the tortilla pinchos before they sell out; mornings are calmest.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps
Celso y Manolo 🚶 12 min★ 4.6 ▾

🕐 Daily 1:00 PM–12:00 AM

C. de la Libertad 1. Tiny and in demand — reservation essential, and tables are time-limited. The deepest fish-and-veggie tapas menu in Chueca: the chuletón de tomate (their famous tomato "steak"), tomato with Cantabrian anchovies, cod croquetas, soldadito de Pavía (battered cod), and rabas are Wil & Joanne's run; meat dishes on the menu cover Mom.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps
Cervecería Cervantes 🚕 taxi ~8 min (🚶 23 min) ▾

🕐 Daily 11:00 AM–11:30 PM

Plaza de Jesús 7. Old-school tiled cervecería, mostly locals — a genuine local favorite. Frame it as a stop on a Prado/Retiro/Las Letras outing rather than a trip of its own. Galician octopus, gambas, fried calamari, and Padrón peppers are the pescatarian orders.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps
Casa Lucas 🚶 ~28 min (🚕 taxi ~9 min)★ 4.4 ▾

🕐 Daily — Lunch 1:00–3:30 PM · Dinner 8:00 PM–12:00 AM · Wed dinner only · Sat–Sun lunch until 4:00 PM

Calle de la Cava Baja 30, La Latina. A tiny taberna pouring since 1997, doing creative tapas from market produce — the pinchos are named after wine regions. Order the Jumilla (spinach-leek pie with prawns), the Binissalem (baked bonito belly with confit vegetables), smoked sardines with tomato, and the prawn-and-vegetable canelón; rabo de toro and solomillo are Mom's. This is your La Latina evening anchor for the Plaza Mayor side of town. Practicalities: the room is tiny and fills instantly — reserve ahead (online bookings only for the 1 PM and 8 PM seatings), and pinchos are served in pairs, so order accordingly.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps
El Cogollo de la Descarga 🚶 ~20 min (or 🚕 taxi ~7 min)★ 4.8 ▾

🕐 1:00 PM–12:00 AM · Hours conflict by source — confirm before going, especially on a Sunday or Monday (most listings show it closed Sun–Mon)

Calle de las Hileras 6, Austrias — a couple of minutes from Plaza Mayor. A traditional Asturian house with proper table service, and it takes reservations — a comfortable format for Mom. Order the pulpo a las brasas (grilled octopus) and gambas al ajillo for Wil & Joanne; the fabada asturiana and the cachopo are Mom's. Pour the Asturian cider the proper way — from a height, a little at a time. This is the sit-down option inside the Plaza Mayor outing cluster.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps

Casual 3

Casa Revuelta 🚕 taxi ~8 min (🚶 25 min)★ 4.4 ▾

🕐 Tue–Sat 10:30 AM–4:00 PM & 7:00–11:00 PM · Sun 10:30 AM–4:00 PM · Closed Mondays

Tiny bar by Plaza Mayor that does one thing perfectly: bacalao rebozado, battered fried salt cod, with a cold caña. Standing room only — a quick stop for Wil and Joanne while Mom rests at a plaza café; pair it with the Plaza Mayor and San Miguel outing.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps
La Casa del Abuelo 🚶 21 min★ 4.3 ▾

🕐 Daily 12:00 PM–12:00 AM

A classic, with rules. It's a 4-location operation now, so go to the original on Calle de la Victoria only. Order the gambas al ajillo and the house wine, decline the extras, and check the bill — upselling and surprise bread charges are documented. Go off-peak.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps
Los Huevos de Lucio 🚶 ~28 min (🚕 taxi ~9 min)★ 4.2 ▾

🕐 Daily 1:00–4:15 PM & 8:00 PM–12:00 AM · Sat–Sun lunch until 4:30 PM

Calle de la Cava Baja 30, La Latina — the casual taberna sibling of Casa Lucio, the famous huevos rotos house at No. 35. Same family, bigger castizo room, friendlier prices (~€30 a head). The huevos rotos are the order (ask for them without chistorra or jamón if needed), plus the tomato tartar and bacalao bites for Wil & Joanne; cochinillo, rabo de toro, and the chuleta are Mom's. Reservations are taken and the queue outside moves fast; wheelchair access is limited. This is the roomy walk-in alternative when Casa Lucas, a few doors away, is full.

Breakfast 1

Café Comercial 🚶 6 min★ 4.3 ▾

🕐 Daily 8:30 AM–1:00 AM (Thu–Sat until 2:00 AM)

Madrid café institution since 1887 on Glorieta de Bilbao — marble tables, mirrors, proper sit-down breakfast. Tostada con tomate or chocolate con churros to start the day; its rice dishes also make it the easy carb-friendly lunch before you leave for Valencia. It's also the one classic here that takes reservations — book ahead to erase any wait for Mom; weekday mornings are calm.

🕐 Daily 8:00 AM–6:00 PM (hours vary by source — check day-of)

The Malasaña original that kicked off Madrid's specialty-coffee scene, on Calle de la Palma. Flat white is the order, plus tostadas and homemade cake. Best for a slow Monday or Tuesday morning.

Calle de las Infantas 25, Chueca — same neighborhood as the hotel. The Danish specialty-coffee and bakery chain's new Madrid outpost, set inside an 1855 building. Dessert 3

Chocolatería San Ginés 🚶 19 min★ 4.3 ▾

🕐 Open 24 hours Thu–Sun & holiday eves · Mon–Wed 8:00 AM–12:00 AM

The churros institution, going since 1894 in a little alley off Sol. Six churros and a cup of thick dipping chocolate is the order — porras (the fat ones) if you're hungry. Go on a weekday morning or late at night to dodge the queue — Thu–Sun it never closes.

🕐 Mon & Wed–Thu 8:00 AM–10:00 PM · Tue 8:00 AM–4:00 PM · Fri–Sat 8:00 AM–11:00 PM · Sun 8:00 AM–10:00 PM

Calle de las Huertas 59, Barrio de las Letras — it recently moved here from Calle Santa María 30, so older lists point at the old address. The locals' alternative to San Ginés, ranked #1 for churros in Madrid in a recent roundup of Spanish food guides: chocolate con churros and porras is the order. Same outing zone as Casa Revuelta and Plaza Mayor. One quirk: Tuesdays it closes at 4:00 PM, so make it a Sunday or Monday stop.

Mercado de San Antón 🚶 9 min★ 4.4 ▾

🕐 Daily 9:30 AM–12:00 AM

Chueca's own market, three floors a few streets from the hotel — real food stalls downstairs, tapas counters above, rooftop terrace on top. This is the one locals actually use. Graze the second floor for lunch on a wander day.

Mercado de San Miguel 🚕 taxi ~8 min (🚶 23 min)★ 4.6 ▾

🕐 Sun–Thu 10:00 AM–12:00 AM · Fri–Sat 10:00 AM–1:00 AM

The famous 1916 iron-and-glass food hall by Plaza Mayor — beautiful, and honestly touristy and pricey, with mostly standing tables. Go once for the spectacle: vermouth and an olive skewer, jamón, Galician oysters. Weekday before noon beats the crowds; pair with Plaza Mayor.

Sightseeing 7

El Retiro Park 🚕 taxi ~10 min★ 4.8 ▾

🕐 Daily 6:00 AM–10:00 PM (winter hours)

Madrid's great green living room — flat shaded paths, the boating lake, and the glass Palacio de Cristal (free to peek in). Take a taxi to the Puerta de Alcalá gate and stroll as much or little as Mom likes; benches and cafés everywhere. Sunday afternoon is when all of Madrid is here.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps
Plaza Mayor 🚶 20 min (or 🚕 taxi ~7 min)★ 4.4 ▾

🕐 Open square, always accessible

The grand 17th-century square — frescoed Casa de la Panadería, arcades, Felipe III on his horse in the middle. Flat and car-free; sit at an arcade café and watch the city go by. Combine with San Miguel and Casa Revuelta in one taxi outing.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps
Templo de Debod 🚕 taxi ~10 min★ 4.6 ▾

🕐 Grounds always open · Interior Tue–Sun 10:00 AM–8:00 PM, closed Mondays

A real 2nd-century BC Egyptian temple in a park above the city. Skip the tiny interior; the move is the park at sunset (about 5:50 PM in early December) as the stone turns gold. Flat paths and benches all around it.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps
Royal Palace & Sabatini Gardens 🚕 taxi ~10 min★ 4.5 ▾

🕐 Palace exterior and plaza always viewable · Sabatini Gardens daily from ~9:00 AM, free

See it the mom-friendly way: the palace façade from the Plaza de la Armería, Almudena Cathedral right opposite, then the formal Sabatini Gardens for hedges, fountains, and statues — no tickets, no queues, no museum marathon. Same taxi run as the Templo de Debod.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps
Almudena Cathedral 🚶 ~20 min or 🚕 taxi ~8 min ▾

🕐 Free entry daily (museum & dome ticket at the door, ~€7)

Madrid's cathedral, finished only in 1993 but built on the old city wall site; the colorful dome interior and the Virgin of Almudena chapel are the highlights. No advance ticket needed — walk in. Pairs with the Royal Palace exterior outing.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps
Descalzas Reales Monastery 🚕 taxi ~8 min ▾

🕐 Guided visits only, Tue–Sun · Closed Mondays · Book online at Patrimonio Nacional

Plaza de las Descalzas. A working royal convent founded in 1559, stuffed with Renaissance art, and the church-iest deep cut in Madrid — and this one is Mom's call, made with the full facts: the guided tour (~1 hour) covers three floors linked only by stairs — it starts up the grand staircase — with no lift or step-free route, and Patrimonio Nacional itself states there is currently no access for people with disabilities. A yes only if she's up for several flights of stairs. Language: Patrimonio's own tour is Spanish-guided and there is no standard Tuesday English slot, so an English visit on Tue Dec 1 (it's closed Mon, and you land Sun) needs a third-party/private booking — third-party English tours run Thu/Fri.

Your home boulevard — the hotel sits just above it. Walk the wide, flat pavements from Callao toward the white Metropolis Building at Calle de Alcalá for the classic Madrid postcard view. Best in the early evening when the theatre marquees light up.

Race 6

Expo Deporte Valencia — Bib Pickup 🚕 taxi ~15–18 min★ 4.0 ▾

🕐 Thu Dec 3 – Sat Dec 5 (2026 hours not yet posted; recent editions ~10:00 AM–8:00 PM — confirm closer to the trip)

Feria Valencia, Av. de les Fires s/n, 46035 Valencia (Pavilion 5). No race-day pickup exists, so this is a hard deadline — go Thu or Fri to beat the Saturday crush. Bring photo ID (or a photo of it) for both runners' bibs and race bags. Getting there (corrected per feriavalencia.com — ⚠️ an earlier version of this card had the wrong metro line): taxi ~15 min is easiest with Mom (feriavalencia.com puts it at 7.4 km / ~15 min driving from Valencia Nord, so expect similar from the apartment). By metro: Metro Line 1 (Llíria–Villanueva de Castellón) to the Carolines-Fira stop, which is ~600 m from the venue entrance — walk time from there not confirmed by the operator, budget ~8–10 min. Bus 62 also runs Benimàmet–Estació Nord and stops at the Feria every 10–15 min, boarding at Estació del Nord (~10-min walk from the apartment first). Confirm the exact walking route once you're on the ground — this card is now sourced to the venue's own transport page, not a prior guess.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps
Marathon Start — Plaça de la Marató 🚊 Line 10 tram from Alacant🚕 taxi ~8 min ▾

🕐 Sun Dec 6 · First wave 8:15 AM, waves to 9:35 AM

The low-stress play is the Metrovalencia Line 10 tram from Alacant station (~5-min walk from base) straight to the Ciutat Arts i Ciències stop — no traffic, no road closures. Board at Alacant: it's the terminus, so trams are empty when you get on. Leave 7:00–7:10 AM and you're at the start zone by ~7:35–7:45. Russafa station (~7 min) is the backup, but trams may arrive packed. A taxi takes ~8 min in normal traffic, but on race morning allow 30. Eat breakfast at the Airbnb before leaving: nothing near base or the start opens early enough on a Sunday.

Use the race's live tracking for Wil and Joanne's exact splits.

🕐 Mon–Sat 1:00–4:00 PM only · Closed Sundays

C/ d'Isabel de Villena 155. The real deal since 1922: paella cooked over an orange-wood fire on the beachfront, eaten from the pan. Order the seafood paella (paella de marisco) — same orange-wood fire — or the vegetable paella for Wil & Joanne; the traditional paella valenciana (chicken & rabbit) is Mom's order. Book well ahead for Saturday Dec 5 lunch — it can't be the post-race meal because it's closed Sundays (confirmed via casa-carmela.com: open Mon–Sat). Wheelchair accessible, which helps Mom.

Valencia Cathedral & the Holy Chalice 🚶 ~17 min ▾

🕐 Ticket €8–10 incl. audio guide (buy online or at the door)

The cathedral's Santo Cáliz chapel holds the agate chalice venerated as the Holy Grail of the Last Supper — for Mom, this is the single most meaningful stop of the whole trip. Skip the Miguelete bell tower (207 steps); the grail chapel, the Renaissance frescoes, and the museum are all on the flat. Next door, the Basílica de la Virgen de los Desamparados (free) holds Valencia's beloved patroness.

🕐 Ticketed entry ~€16 with audio guide · Closed Mondays

Calle Caballeros 35, old town. They call it the Valencian Sistine Chapel: a plain Gothic church outside, 2,000 m² of restored Baroque frescoes covering every inch inside. Small, seated, and overwhelming in the best way — a Mom highlight. Book online; fits the Thu/Fri old-town days.

Packs out fast; go right at opening.

Carrer de Mallorca 401. For Mom, the interior is a MUST, not an optional extra — the light through the stained glass is unlike any church she has seen. Note: Tue Dec 8 is the Feast of the Immaculate Conception, a national holiday — expect special Masses and some closures that day.

Transport 2

Universitat Metro (Plaça Universitat) 🚶 ~6 min flat ▾

🕐 ~5:00 AM–midnight (later Fri, all night Sat)

Your interchange: L1 (red) and L2 (purple) — L2 runs direct to Sagrada Família and Sant Antoni, L1 to Plaça Catalunya. Handy for the runners, but with Mom and luggage, taxis are cheap and door-to-door; treat the metro as the backup, not the plan.

Sants Station → Hotel by Taxi 🚕 taxi ~10–12 min from the rank ▾

🕐 Taxis at the rank throughout train hours

Arrival day (Tue Dec 8) you roll in by train — skip the metro change with suitcases and tired legs and take a taxi straight to Carrer de Muntaner 2. Settle in, then dinner is a 3-minute walk: La Flauta or El Racó d'en Cesc.

Shopping 6

SVD — sivasdescalzo 🚶 ~23 min (or 🚕 taxi ~8 min)★ 4.1 ▾

🕐 Mon–Sat 11:00 AM–8:00 PM

Carrer de Bailèn 18, Eixample — the flagship of Spain's premier sneaker retailer: limited drops run through its raffle app. It's also a Stüssy stockist, making it Barcelona's Stüssy route since the city has no chapter store.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps
24 Kilates 🚶 ~25 min (or 🚕 taxi ~9 min) ▾

🕐 Mon–Fri 10:00 AM–6:00 PM · Closed weekends · Hours conflict by source — confirm before going

Carrer del Comerç 29, El Born — a Barcelona streetwear icon since 2005, famous for its own collaboration sneakers with ASICS, New Balance and Mizuno. Slots into the Born day.

Limited Editions 🚶 ~14 min★ 2.9 ▾

🕐 Mon–Sat 11:30 AM–9:00 PM

Carrer del Duc 13, Gothic Quarter — a limited-sneaker institution near the Cathedral, but recent reviews run weak. Frame it honestly: a browse rather than a pilgrimage.

Foot District 🚶 ~16 min ▾

🕐 Tue–Sat 11:30 AM–7:30 PM · Hours conflict by source — confirm before going

Carrer de la Lleona 4, Gothic Quarter — premium sneaker boutique a few streets from Limited Editions; the two pair up as one Gothic-quarter shopping stop.

🍎 Apple Maps🗺 Google Maps
L'Espai — Bandit x Odda 🚶 ~17 min (or 🚕 taxi ~6 min) ▾

🕐 Opened Oct 1, 2026 · Hours not yet listed — check @oddarunning before going

Carrer de Pau Claris 126, Eixample — Bandit Running's first European flagship, opened October 1, 2026 in partnership with Madrid's Odda. Two doors, one into each brand, an in-store-only Bandit x Odda capsule, and a runners' clubhouse inside: coworking space, sauna, cold plunge and showers. A must-stop.

Bikila Barcelona 🚕 taxi ~10 min (🚶 ~28 min)★ 4.8 ▾

🕐 Mon–Fri 10:30 AM–2:00 PM & 5:00–8:30 PM · Sat 10:00 AM–2:30 PM

Passeig de Pujades 7, by Ciutadella Park — the Barcelona branch of Bikila, Spain's running institution (see Madrid). Pairs with a Ciutadella / Born day.

Good to know
  • Flights and both hotels are booked. The two trains (AVE Dec 2, Euromed Dec 8) are the last tickets to grab.
  • TAP fare includes carry-on and meals; checked bags are extra. Seat selection was pay-extra — free assignment opens at check-in.
  • Spain is 6 hours ahead of New York. We land back at JFK, not Newark.
  • Paella is lunch, never dinner — and in Valencia, book it and pre-order it.
